A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MotionSight, MotionVid-QA and MotionChat. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original MotionSight benchmark results and ablations in Tables 2–4, plus MotionChat fine-tuning results in Appendix D and Table S3.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds general-video, captioning, video-generation, robustness and model-scaling results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Equation (1) drops the optional object-motion response input from the specified camera-inference procedure. The core grounding/tracking, visual spotlight and motion-blur pipeline remains, as does the SFT/DPO training recipe already documented in v1. MotionChat is not a newly introduced architecture.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained MotionBench and FAVOR-Bench evaluations, v2 adds VideoMME general-video understanding, TempCompass including captioning, and text-to-video generation evaluated with VBench. This substantially broadens task coverage. MotionVid-QA's reported sources and 40K-video/87K-QA scale remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes GLM-4V-Plus, MiniCPM-V2.6, PLLaVA-34B and CogVLM2-Video. Table 3 reduces open-source baseline rows from fifteen to four, removing comparisons including Aria, Tarsier and Video-LLaVA. V2 also adds a direct-coordinate prompting comparator and the Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B generation baseline.

E3.justification: Existing MotionBench/FAVOR-Bench splits and retained models' frame budgets remain unchanged. New experimental designs include TempCompass grading with gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, VBench generation metrics, separate SFT and SFT+DPO controls, InternVL3 scaling from 1B to 78B, and controlled darkening/window/decay sweeps. These expand evaluation procedures substantially.

E4.justification: V2 adds training-stage ablation, background-darkening and blur-parameter sensitivity tests, model-size scaling, direct-coordinate prompting controls, and Grad-CAM analyses (Table 4, Tables 11–14, Figures 7, 11 and 14). The original visual-prompt ablation remains as Table 6; several qualitative examples are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. V2's additional experiments continue reporting point estimates; its parameter sweeps do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Common MotionSight benchmark scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds extensive results, including VideoMME 76.0% versus its 73.7% baseline and TempCompass captioning 64.0 versus 54.6. V1 presents MotionChat's 45.8% FAVOR-Bench result as its full model; v2 labels that row SFT-only and adds 48.3% for SFT+DPO. This is revised stage/result reporting, not an established same-setting gain. MotionChat's MotionBench results and numerous baseline/category entries are omitted.

T1.justification: V2 adds an explicit product-form temporal-weight definition in Equation (7), replacing v1's geometric-series characterization. It also corrects the zero-padding condition below Equation (5) from t-k <= 1 to s_t-k < 1. Existing aggregation, DPO and dataset-subset mathematics remains; no substantial theoretical framework or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central zero-shot prompting and large-scale dataset contributions remain. V2 elevates MotionChat into the abstract and introduction, adding the claim that its 7B model achieves 48.3% FAVOR-Bench accuracy, comparable to Qwen2.5VL-72B's 48.1%. V1 discussed MotionChat's utility only in the appendix without this comparison.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations based on spotlight-like pretraining imagery, attention visualizations, coordinate-parsing difficulty and captioning's greater descriptive demands. Appendix D discusses runtime/performance tradeoffs. Appendix G replaces v1's inherited-bias and misuse limitations with detector-domain dependence and diminished benefits in object-free scenes, substantially revising applicability discussion.

D1.justification: V2 discloses the blur-weight implementation, the TempCompass evaluator identifier, conversion of SFT data into video-text pairs for generation, and an inference-overhead estimate below 75%. Existing hardware, batch size, detection thresholds, default prompting parameters and annotation instructions are retained. The project URL and code/data-release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds VideoAgent and VideoTree to contextualize computational overhead and removes the Aria and Video-LLaVA references. The principal positioning against existing video models, motion datasets and image-derived visual prompting remains. The switch to author-year citations is stylistic.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes existing material: benchmark descriptions and comparisons are merged, MotionChat moves into the main experimental narrative, and its former appendix material is redistributed. The standalone supplement becomes integrated appendices. Introduction and method passages are condensed or rewritten, with changed headings and citation style throughout.

P2.justification: V2 redraws pipeline Figures 2 and 4, compresses FAVOR-Bench Table 3, and adds attention, scaling and generation displays. Existing content is also redistributed: v1 Figure 5 becomes v2 Figures 5 and 15, while v1 Figure 7 is split across Figures 9 and 13 with an added baseline comparison. Wrapped tables, prompt boxes and document styling change substantially.

improvement.justification: V1 largely leaves parameter sensitivity, scaling and transfer beyond motion QA untested. V2's controlled ablations and general-video, captioning and generation evaluations substantially strengthen evidence for robustness and utility, while detector and runtime discussions clarify practical constraints. Reduced baseline/detail reporting and the unexplained MotionChat result relabeling are drawbacks, but the added diagnostic evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
